text:
luis martinez: hi all, new hire here. received an M1 Max MBP and did the ABM/Kandji flow. Kandji says enrolled but macOS shows 'System extension blocked' for our VPN and Keychain has no 'Redwood Corporate CA'. when I try to enable FileVault i get 'Escrow failed: network unreachable'. Okta device trust shows untrusted. set up on hotel wifi during onboarding — could that be it? who should I ping?
it-answers: welcome luis :wave: hotel/captive portals often break the cert/SCEP step. quick checks: which network did you use (you said hotel), run:
```
profiles status -type enrollment
sudo fdesetup status
```
and check Keychain Access -> Certificates for any Redwood CA. don't paste full serials here; last 4 is fine if we need to push remediation.
luis martinez: outputs:
profiles status -type enrollment: Enrolled to kandji: true; com.redwood.mdm present; com.redwood.security missing
sudo fdesetup status: FileVault is Off
Keychain: no Redwood CA
sophia lee: yep that explains Okta. first try: connect to a network without captive portal (RWD-Corp or phone hotspot) and visit https://kandji.redwood/setup-cert in Safari to force the CA. if captive portal intercepted the initial SCEP flow it won't have installed the intermediate cert. once cert present run `profiles renew -type enrollment`.
oncall-bot: automated hint: if system time is off SCEP can fail. run `sudo systemsetup -getusingnetworktime`
luis martinez: i'm remote and won't be at office today. tried tethering to phone but hotspot was flaky, kept dropping. i changed DNS to 1.1.1.1 and retried the Kandji cert URL, got an 'Untrusted Certificate' prompt and accepted. profiles renew shows com.redwood.security present now but `sudo fdesetup enable` still returns 'Escrow failed: TLS handshake failed'. Okta still non-compliant. last 4 serial: B12F
it-answers: TLS handshake error is often our SCEP/escrow endpoint being blocked by hotel network or the phone hotspot messing with MTU. two options: 1) we can grant a 2-hour temporary admin window and push a remediation that performs a manual escrow via our internal portal (we record the recovery key), or 2) we can provide a one-time recovery key through the IT portal if you're comfortable with that audited flow. which do you prefer?
\lsuis martinez: option 1 please, temp admin sounds fine. blocked on installing dev tools anyway.
it-answers: temporary admin granted for 2 hours. creating ticket NH-20260422-09 and tagging endpoint. pushing remediation: install com.redwood.security (if missing) and run escrow via portal. please stay online for ~10 minutes.
 sophia lee: also, after we fix escrow, you'll likely need to approve the VPN system extension under System Settings -> Privacy & Security. i'll also watch for the device in console.
oncall-bot: remediation action: push_profile(com.redwood.security) -> delivered -> device acknowledged. escrow attempt via portal -> success.
luis martinez: saw the Kandji action popup, approved it. portal flow gave me a recovery key and `fdesetup` now reports FileVault On. Okta switched to compliant after a sync. VPN extension approval still pending; clicked allow in Privacy & Security and VPN connected. all good now — thanks everyone! :rocket:
